newsitem.title: UK: Firmer dollar hampers London gold, white metals slip.
newsitem.headline: Firmer dollar hampers London gold, white metals slip.

text.p: A stronger dollar on Monday afternoon limited interest in gold while speculators sent platinum and palladium (PGMs) sliding in New York, dealers said.

The dollar strengthed in Europe on concerns for the strength of European Monetary Union (EMU) following last week's row between the German government and the Bundesbank over revaluing its gold and a socialist election win in France at the weekend
Gold was fixed at $343.90 down just 10 cents from this morning and $345.60 on Friday afternoon.

The dollar had firmed last week after the German government and the Bundesbank rowed over revaluing gold reserves. The foreign exchange markets saw Bonn's plan to plug budget gaps with the proceeds as a potential fudge of the EMU rules.
The French poll result was seen as potentially damaging for a European single currency in 1999 as a Socialist government may not adhere as strongly to an EMU austerity policy as its predecessor.
Some dealers dismissed as a PGM price issue the visit of officials from Almaz, the Russian export agency to belated negotiations on starting delayed 1997 exports to their Japanese customers.
"The Russians have said this before. The volatility today is not particularly connected with Almaz," one dealer said.
Platinum fixed $7.00 down on the morning fix at $398.50 per ounce and palladium was $9.00 weaker at $172.00 with both metals having slipped lower before attracting buying.
Dealers said the markets were pretty thin giving plenty of scope to the Nymex locals. "Its choppy and nervous and any bit of sizeable business will move it quite a bit," one dealer said.
Almaz officials in Tokyo said they would be delivering metal to Japanese customers, their biggest buyers, in June but dealers said the market would ignore that and remain nervous.
"Until we see physical metal begin to flow this is the way it is going to be," one said.
Lease rates meanwhile for platinum and palladium remained high demonstrating the continuing tightness of the markets.
Platinum was quoted at around 35 percent for a month down to 20 percent for six months and palladium was indicated at 40 percent and 24 percent.
Russia, the largest export of palladium and second biggest supplier of platinum, has not exported since December last year due to political and administrative problems.
Silver was a couple of cents easier at $4.71/$4.73.
